findings.summary: No anchor test pins the new critic prompt wording; criterion 2's demonstration overstates what the lib.rs anchor test covers
findings.evidence: The anchor table in lib.rs has verifier rows for the field (605, 612) but no critic row naming request_reading_mismatch or its replacement. critic.md line 5 is the only place the critic is told about the field. The demonstration says 'The lib.rs anchor test fails if a prompt lacks the new wording', which holds only for verifier.md. Fix: Add critic rows to the anchor table, such as ("critic", "set request_misread true only") and ("critic", "other remarks about the reading go in findings"), so the critic wording required by criterion 2 is checked by cargo test.

findings.summary: The pbvc planning replay fails only if critic_round copies the reason into the stored field; it does not test end_round's branch on its own
findings.evidence: Under the plan, critic_round stores request_reading_mismatch only when request_misread is true. With the boolean false, an end_round that still tested the stored field for Some would pass the replay. Only a regression that stores or tests request_misread_reason would make it fail. The 'fails without' text names both end_round and critic_round, which is broader than the test shows. Fix: Narrow the 'fails without' text to the reason-to-stored mapping and the boolean branch. Also assert directly in the test that the stored critique's request_reading_mismatch is None even though a non-empty reason was given (already planned), and keep the true-misread planning test as the check on end_round's branch.

findings.summary: The send_back.rs VerdictOutput literal is test scaffolding, not a production caller
findings.evidence: The literal at send_back.rs:462 builds a fixed VerdictOutput next to a fixed CheckRun and calls judge as a test does. The files list calls it 'test-module', but the dependents entry calls it 'the send-back caller'. Fix: Use one label in both places: a test-module literal.

summary: The plan meets the request and the accepted reading. It swaps the free-text field for a required boolean plus an optional reason in CriticOutput and VerdictOutput, makes end_round and judge branch only on the boolean, and keeps the stored record field, set only when the boolean is true, so records.rs and its readers are unchanged. I searched the snapshot for request_reading_mismatch: the plan's sites match it, covering every agent-JSON fixture (fake.rs, run/tests.rs, run_pin_tests.rs, scope_guard.rs, cli common/lifecycle/introspection/retry/drain/job_plan), the three struct literals (send_back.rs, verify.rs, outputs.rs), the record readers (retry.rs, status.rs, status/planning.rs, display.rs) and the record-shaped fixtures. I read end_round/critic_round (planning.rs:409-491), judge (verify.rs:625-637), the REQUIRED_FIELDS check and clause splitter (verify.rs:1246-1386), the verifier redaction and stored field (verification.rs:350-424), harden (outputs.rs:581), and the run/tests.rs helpers. All exist as the plan describes. The proposed anchor 'set request_misread true' passes has_anchor, because clause_words keeps underscores and lowercases. The verifier prompt grows by about 31 tokens (estimate, not measured), within the 67 tokens of headroom. D181 is unused. Keeping the major finding only in judge matches D93's text (decisions.md:2084-2085). The replay tests map the recorded 'None…' openings into the reason with the boolean false, a fair replay given that old JSON can no longer parse, and the plan says so openly. Remaining issues are minor: the critic prompt's new wording has no anchor test, and the planning replay only fails if the reason-to-stored mapping regresses. Athena's out-of-deliverables findings are already justified in the plan's files list.
